title: Typerclass: Model Training and Evaluation Report
text: following indicators used model, along brief description : n_unique_values – Number unique values variable (excluding missing values). std_dev – Standard deviation; measures spread values . max_relative_frequency – Proportion frequent value relative total number observations. norm_entropy – Normalized entropy; measures evenly values distributed. min_value – Minimum observed value. max_value – Maximum observed value. range_value – Difference maximum minimum values. shannon_entropy – Shannon entropy; measure uncertainty information content. simpson_index – Simpson diversity index; indicates concentrated values . skewness_probs – Skewness value-probability distribution; measures asymmetry. kurtosis_probs – Excess kurtosis value distribution; indicates tail heaviness. dispersion_index – Variance--mean ratio value probabilities; measures dispersion. uniformity – Shannon entropy normalized log(n_unique_values); measures distributional evenness. top2_ratio – Sum probabilities two frequent values. top3_ratio – Sum probabilities three frequent values. table provides overview indicators used model. indicators missing values, ensuring reliable inputs training. exception dispersion_index, contains 128 missing values. ranger package can handle missing values default; preliminary tests also showed imputation improve model performance.
code: # Data import & preparation  # Import dataset data <- read_csv("./vignettes/model_data.csv") #> Rows: 1167 Columns: 18 #> ── Column specification ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> Delimiter: "," #> chr  (3): variable, dataset, type #> dbl (15): n_unique_values, std_dev, max_relative_frequency, norm_entropy, mi... #>  #> ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data. #> ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message.  # Balanced sample set.seed(123)  data_N <- data %>%   filter(type == "N") %>%   sample_n(400)  data_O <- data %>%   filter(type == "O") %>%   sample_n(200)  data_S <- data %>%   filter(type == "S")  data <- bind_rows(data_N, data_O, data_S)   # Split into training (80%) and test (20%) sets, stratified by 'type' set.seed(123) data_split <- initial_split(data, prop = 0.8, strata = type) train_data <- training(data_split) test_data <- testing(data_split)  # Fix consistent class level ordering for the whole script class_order <- c("N", "O", "S")  indicators <- train_data %>%   select(-dataset, -variable, -type) %>%   colnames()  df_indicators <- tibble(indicator = indicators)   # --- NA count per indicator  na_table <- train_data %>%   select(all_of(indicators)) %>%   summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.)))) %>%   pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "indicator", values_to = "na_count") %>%   arrange(desc(na_count))  na_table %>%   gt() %>%   tab_header(     title = "Overview of Indicators and Missing Values"   ) %>%   cols_label(     indicator = "Indicator",     na_count = "NAs"   )

title: Typerclass: Model Training and Evaluation Report
text: tested preprocessing approach using median imputation numeric predictors. However, preliminary tests showed improvement model performance, decided proceed recipe without imputation. Random Forest XGBoost selected evaluated hyperparameter tuning. selected mtry range using classic rule--thumb centered sqrt(p), p number predictors, expanded ±50% allow slightly simpler complex splits. XGBoost specified using gradient-boosted tree model tunable hyperparameters. used xgboost engine set model classification mode predict three classes. tuned XGBoost using cross-validation folds Random Forest. mtry range follows rule--thumb (centered sqrt(p)), hyperparameters use typical ranges boosted trees.
code: # Define Preprocessing Recipes  # (A) Recipe with no imputation rec_none <- recipe(type ~ ., data = train_data) %>%   update_role(dataset, variable, new_role = "info") # Model Specifications  # ---- Random Forest ---- rf_spec <- rand_forest(   trees = tune(),   mtry = tune(),   min_n = tune() ) %>%   set_engine("ranger", importance = "permutation") %>%   set_mode("classification") # Create workflow combining recipe + model rf_tune_wf <- workflow() %>%   add_recipe(rec_none) %>% # change rec_median here for imputation   add_model(rf_spec)  # 5-fold cross-validation (stratified) set.seed(123) cv_folds <- vfold_cv(train_data, v = 5, strata = type)  # Define regular grid for RF tuning p <- ncol(train_data %>% select(-dataset, -variable, -type)) mtry_center <- floor(sqrt(p)) mtry_low <- max(1L, floor(mtry_center * 0.5)) mtry_high <- min(p, ceiling(mtry_center * 1.5))  rf_grid <- grid_space_filling(   trees(range = c(300L, 1000L)),   mtry(range = c(mtry_low, mtry_high)),   min_n(range = c(2L, 20L)),   size = 20 )  # Run grid search for RF rf_tune_res <- tune_grid(   rf_tune_wf,   resamples = cv_folds,   grid = rf_grid,   metrics = metric_set(accuracy) )   # Select best parameters based on accuracy best_rf_params <- select_best(rf_tune_res, metric = "accuracy") best_rf_params %>%   gt() %>%   tab_header(     title = "Best Random Forest Hyperparameters"   ) %>%   fmt_number(     columns = everything(),     decimals = 2   ) # Finalize model with best parameters rf_final_spec <- finalize_model(rf_spec, best_rf_params)  rf_final_wf <- workflow() %>%   add_recipe(rec_none) %>%   add_model(rf_final_spec)  # Fit the tuned RF on the full training data rf_final_fit <- rf_final_wf %>%   fit(data = train_data) # ---- XGBoost ---- xgb_spec <- boost_tree(   trees = tune(),   tree_depth = tune(),   learn_rate = tune(),   loss_reduction = tune(),   min_n = tune(),   sample_size = tune(),   mtry = tune() ) %>%   set_engine("xgboost") %>%   set_mode("classification") # Create workflow combining recipe + model xgb_tune_wf <- workflow() %>%   add_recipe(rec_none) %>%   add_model(xgb_spec)  # Define regular grid for XGBoost tuning p <- ncol(train_data %>% select(-dataset, -variable, -type)) mtry_center <- floor(sqrt(p)) mtry_low <- max(1L, floor(mtry_center * 0.5)) mtry_high <- min(p, ceiling(mtry_center * 1.5))  xgb_params <- extract_parameter_set_dials(xgb_spec) %>%   update(     trees = trees(range = c(300L, 1000L)),     tree_depth = tree_depth(range = c(2L, 10L)),     learn_rate = learn_rate(range = c(0.01, 0.3)),     loss_reduction = loss_reduction(range = c(0.0, 5.0)),     min_n = min_n(range = c(2L, 20L)),     sample_size = sample_prop(range = c(0.5, 1.0)),     mtry = mtry(range = c(mtry_low, mtry_high))   )  xgb_grid <- grid_space_filling(   xgb_params,   size = 20 )  # Run grid search for XGBoost xgb_tune_res <- tune_grid(   xgb_tune_wf,   resamples = cv_folds,   grid = xgb_grid,   metrics = metric_set(accuracy) )   # Select best parameters based on accuracy best_xgb_params <- select_best(xgb_tune_res, metric = "accuracy") best_xgb_params %>%   gt() %>%   tab_header(     title = "Best XGBoost Hyperparameters"   ) %>%   fmt_number(     columns = everything(),     decimals = 3   ) # Finalize model with best parameters xgb_final_spec <- finalize_model(xgb_spec, best_xgb_params)  xgb_final_wf <- workflow() %>%   add_recipe(rec_none) %>%   add_model(xgb_final_spec)  # Fit the tuned XGBoost on the full training data xgb_final_fit <- xgb_final_wf %>%   fit(data = train_data)

title: Predicts Types of Variables
text: goal Typerclass predict type variables (nominal, ordinal, scale) based empirical distribution observed values. Numeric variables processed probabilistic prediction model. numeric inputs, typerclass analyzes empirical distribution observed values returns: predicted measurement type (.pred_class) estimated probabilities class: .pred_N (Nominal) .pred_O (Ordinal) .pred_S (Scale) predicted class corresponds measurement level highest estimated probability. Variables type factor first converted numeric processed probabilistic prediction model. Variables type logical, character, date excluded probabilistic prediction model. variables deterministically classified Nominal, since measurement level inferred empirical numeric distribution. variables: .pred_class set N (Nominal) .pred_N, .pred_O, .pred_S returned NA Variables types (e.g. complex, list) processed prediction results returned NA output fields.
